I donno how basic is necessary so i'll be pretty low level. With realistic and sim battles, (RB and SB) Altitude is your friend, always try to climb as fast and high as you can at the beginning if you are fighter ing. It's less important to have the altitude advantage in Arcade but still can be helpful. With altitude over your enemy, your options are more open. If your lower, especially as Americans and non-spit British, you are quite vulnerable to attacks from all the nations you face.

Keep in mind, I'm speaking generally to each nation, so specific planes can vary.

With the Americans you'll want to use their speed to your advantage and avoid turning as much as you can while fighting. For British, the typhoons/hurricanes are like the Americans, more for speed and energy fighting, (using your speed and altitude energy advantage to fight). The Spitfires are generally good turn fighters, (usually what one thinks about for a "dog fight", sharp turns and more aerobatic maneuvers). Knowing these advantages will help a little bit.

What I think is the best way to improve is to know your enemy planes and how they match up to yours. this can take a while and will start out helping quickly but then slow progress starts as you begin learning more specific situations like how a certain plane turns better at a lower speed, or begins to drop of in performance at certain altitudes. knowing your plane and others comes from either flying all the planes and seeing how they fly in different situations or seeing how someone killed you or you killed someone else.

Again in general,

American's can't turn well, but have good speeds and decent armament and diving. So they are well suited for Boom and Zooming, (Using a higher altitude to dive on the enemy, "booming" them with your guns and "zooming" up and away with your gained speed to back to your higher altitude). When boom and zooming it can be tempting to chase the enemy too much and lose your speed from to much turning, this can energy trap you leaving you vulnerable to a more maneuverable plane, so try to keep your speed, so you can trade it back for altitude or running away to teammates.

British have the typhoons/hurricanes which are similar to the Americans, and the spitfires that are quite good turn fighters, and are well armed. The spits can out-turn most planes, so they are good for energy trapping others and lighting them up. I would be careful with turning against the Japs though, the A6M# or "Zeros" series of planes are very good turn fighters and can out turn pretty much everything in the game (I think one spit can out turn some of the zeros). So be wary of A6M2 or A6M3, etc.

The Russians have Lagg/La series that are good energy fighters like the Americans, and the Ishak line withe I-185 are similar to that but I think slightly worse around tiers 3-4. The Yak line is a very good series for war thunder meta and newer players. They have lower ammo counts but have strong guns. A jack of all trades but master of none. They can be more versatile and have few weakness but few strengths. Their Strength is the ability to use enemy planes weakness better than them. So examples, turning against Americans and boom and zooming against zeros.

Germans mostly have good energy fighters, the 109 series turns better than the 190 series, Both have good armament, i think the FW-190s have a bit better, but the nose mounted cannon on the 109s are great for accurate death. usually wanna stick to Boom and Zoom with these, maybe turning with the 109s. Again here's where knowing the enemy comes into play, along with knowing the plane. So If I recall correctly, 109s can turn, but are better turners at higher speeds and can get roasted if they turn at lower speeds.

Now the Japs. I lovingly refer to them as the paper mache or "pooper macho" planes. They in general are good for turn fighting, especially the Zero series (A6M2, A6M3, A6M5). Their guns tend to be a little week and have low ammo counts. The tree with the Ki-43s and stuff are not quite as good at turning and are the Jap's boom and zoomers. Well not entirely, I believe the Ki-43 III is good for climbing and getting to bombers and reducing energy fighters advantage. the Ki-63? is kinda 190/p-51 mix to me, so Boom and Zoom.

Again,

TL;DR: learn your plane and your enemy's plane.
